note: Every number or assertion that may appear in the paper must be registered here first. `tools/check_claims.py` fails the build if a claim is marked measured without evidence on disk, or if a comparative claim has no control group. Status 'planned' is honest: this repo ships the framework and its offline tests, not a executed study.

claims.statement: The strict JSON Schema gate rejects a mistyped Harbor TaskConfig key (e.g. `cpu` where `cpus` is meant) instead of letting pydantic silently drop it.
The golden Harbor task fixture cross-validates against real harbor 0.24.0 when it is installed, and the gate reports UNVERIFIED rather than passing when it is absent.
The dual-use denylist blocks packaging of a task whose objective matches it, fail-closed, before any model is consulted.
Resuming a completed run issues zero backend calls; no stage is silently re-executed.
Every Stage 1-4 metric returns None on empty input instead of 0.0, so an empty set can never be read as a score of zero.
The held-out split is bound to a corpus digest before any training; a later corpus change makes the lock fail verification instead of drifting.
Shortcut probing is reported in both directions (success DOWN, detection UP) so a defect rate cannot be transcribed into a table as a win.
Every CLI command family has an offline green path: no model, no Docker, no network.
Constructed environments build and run at a rate comparable to human-authored Harbor tasks on the same paper sample (paper 4.1).
claims.control: human-authored Harbor tasks built from the same paper sample

claims.statement: Baselines re-derived by the Reproduction agent agree with the numbers reported in the source papers (paper 4.1).
claims.control: paper-reported metric as reference, tolerance declared per environment

claims.statement: Domain experts approve constructed environments at a rate above the random-paper control (paper 4.1).
claims.control: environments built from randomly sampled off-topic papers, reviewed blind

claims.statement: Trivial shortcut strategies are caught by the constructed evaluators (paper 4.1).
claims.control: same evaluators probed with the reference solution (must pass) as the positive control

claims.statement: Agents improve after the first attempt within an environment, with no weight updates (paper 4.2).
claims.control: same model and environment, no inherited notes or code from the previous attempt

claims.statement: In a majority of environments some model exceeds the reproduced baseline (paper 4.2).
claims.control: reproduced baseline score for the same environment

claims.statement: Between-model variance exceeds between-harness variance on the constructed grid (paper 4.3).
claims.control: the same models under the baseline harness configuration, complete rectangular grid only

claims.statement: Environments built from auto-selected papers outperform environments built from randomly selected papers on held-out benchmarks (paper 4.4).
claims.control: random_environment arm and no_environment arm, identical training recipe

claims.statement: Adding the Review agent improves held-out scores over un-reviewed auto-built environments (paper 4.4).
claims.control: auto_environment arm without human review, identical training recipe

claims.statement: Held-out 2025-2026 papers share no long n-gram spans with the training corpus, so Stage 4 gains are interpretable (paper 4.4).
claims.control: same probe run against pre-cutoff papers as a positive control for the detector
